Meta today announced the launch of several AI-powered devices, including the palm-sized device Muse Charm, designed for its new Muse AI assistant. Details are as follows.

Meta expands AI smart glasses lineup

Meta today kicked off its annual Meta Connect 2026 conference, showcasing its latest achievements in AI technology, wearable devices and VR products.

Last year's most notable release was the Meta Ray-Ban Display, the company's first smart glasses with a built-in display that can show messages, navigation, Meta AI interactive responses and more.

At the time, Meta's AI smart glasses had already received significant market response, with Meta and EssilorLuxottica selling over 7 million pairs combined throughout the year.

However, since then, Meta glasses equipped with cameras have been controversial in terms of privacy and ethics, with extensive discussions across society about privacy, ethics and the broader backlash against AI.

Meta today released Ray-Ban Meta Audio, its first smart glasses without a camera, priced from US$349, available from October 13.

Ray-Ban Meta Audio retains music and podcast playback, calls, real-time translation and other features, offering the same rich audio experience as the camera-equipped version, and supports Meta's recently launched personal AI assistant Muse.

In addition, Meta also unveiled Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 3) tonight, featuring a slimmer design, battery life of up to nine hours, and a new shortcut button, while retaining the 12-megapixel camera and 3K video recording introduced in the previous generation.

Users can customise the new button within the Meta AI app to launch Meta AI or other features with a single tap, such as real-time translation. Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 3) is available from today, priced from US$449.

At tonight's event, Meta also unveiled Meta VR Glasses, a VR headset weighing only about 100 grams and looking more like regular glasses. The device features what Meta calls a "5K Infinite Display built with micro-OLED panels," has built-in Meta AI, supports eye and hand tracking, and relies on a small pocket-sized base for computing, power and storage.

Meta positions VR Glasses as a personal cinema, esports device and workspace, emphasising that it is the first VR device certified with IMAX Enhanced, supporting 3D movies and immersive live sports events.

Alongside Meta VR Glasses, Meta also introduced a new holographic feature that can generate a realistic virtual avatar reflecting the user's expressions and reactions in real time during video calls.

Meta stated that some of these features will also be brought to Meta Ray-Ban Display in the future, allowing users to create a digital face for hands-free video calls, with WhatsApp being the first to support it.

Meta VR Glasses will go on sale in spring 2027, priced at US$1,299.99.

To summarise tonight's glasses product news, Meta has also expanded its Meta Glasses lineup, adding two new styles—Capri and Nova—along with a new collection designed in collaboration with LISA, and launching the Meta Adventurer at US$249, the most affordable smart glasses to date.

The company also simultaneously released a limited-edition Meta Fury style, as well as a new Ivory colourway in collaboration with Kylie Jenner.

Meta unveils Muse Charm

At tonight's event, Meta also announced Muse Charm, a palm-sized device tailor-made for its recently launched personal AI assistant Muse. Meta rolled out the Muse app earlier this month, and it quickly rose to the top of the US App Store and Google Play charts.

According to Bloomberg, Muse Charm was developed by Meta's newly established design lab, led by former Apple interface design chief Alan Dye, in collaboration with the company's Superintelligence AI team.

Muse Charm is described by Meta as a "holdable device," featuring approximately a 2-inch OLED touchscreen with a customisable Muse character at the centre of the interface. Users can change its appearance, outfit, voice and other attributes, and interact directly with Muse through the device.

The device also has built-in front and rear cameras, speakers, microphones, 5G connectivity and a USB-C port. The cameras can be used to take photos and videos, but Bloomberg noted that their primary purpose is to provide visual information for Muse to perform analysis and AI-assisted operations, rather than serving as a traditional camera.

Users can set up and sync through the Muse app on iPhone or Android. When two Charm devices are placed near each other, they can also recognise each other and interact.

Meta plans to officially launch Muse Charm in December. The company has not yet announced pricing, but Bloomberg expects it to be priced similarly to a smartwatch.
